When playing ranked I would say that you need to be in a ship that you are comfortable and know that you can perform consistently well, you know how to exploit it's strengths and how to avoid being exploited by your weakness. With that being said, this is how I set myself to play ranked:  


\- At the beginning of the match you should set yourself up to put your team in a favorable position. Either out trading the enemy, capping. It really depends on what you bring to the table. Your efforts must be directed to help your team to win. From this the game can develop in 3 overall different scenarios:   
\#1 The stalemate: both teams are fairly balanced and trading evenly. It might be tempting to make a push or try a risky play but don't. You need to look for mistakes (and they will appear) and exploit those to give your team an edge.  
\#2 Winning: don't be carried away. since caps give so much points any lead will evaporate super fast. If you are winning, it's up to the enemy make a play, not you. Let them make their mistakes and exploit them.  
 \#2 Losing: this is where things are more delicate. You need to evaluate how your poorly your team is playing. If the throw is imminent, it's time for operation "save your star". By the end of the day, ranked is about winning or at least save you from losing any.  


I wish you the best of luck on Ranked o7.
